title: Normalising Work-from-home Arrangements in Aftermath of COVID-19 Pandemic
what_it_is: Normalising Work-from-home Arrangements in Aftermath of COVID-19 Pandemic

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements advocacy
sections.summary: MOM will keep advocating flexible work arrangements; in 2019 about 85% of employers offered some form, and over 7,000 companies adopted the Tripartite Standard.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: MOM will continue to advocate for the implementation of flexible work arrangements, or FWAs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In 2019, about 85% of employers offered some form of formal or ad hoc FWAs in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: More than 7,000 companies have also adopted the Tripartite Standard on FWAs.

sections.label: Work-from-home consultation challenges
sections.summary: WFH has benefits but also new challenges, and consultations with employers and employees are ongoing to make WFH more sustainable in the steady state.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Indeed, while there are clear benefits of WFH and of continuing with it, it also has a set of new challenges that we are learning about.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We are in the process of consultation with employers and employees to look at how we can moderate and also put in place recommendations to make WFH more sustainable in the steady state.

sections.label: No 2019 WFH data
sections.summary: For 2019, the speaker does not have data on what percentage of the 85% of employers offered WFH arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: For 2019, I do not have the data off-hand on what percentage of the 85% of the employers offered WFH arrangements as well.

sections.label: Discussions on WFH levels
sections.summary: Whether 50% is correct requires proper conversations with tripartite partners, aiming for optimal conditions for sustainable WFH rather than pegging a level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: As to whether 50% is the correct level or not, I think we have to have proper conversations and discussions, hopefully with the tripartite partners to understand better the challenges that come along with WFH – both for the employers as well as for the employees, just as Dr Wan Rizal had mentioned earlier on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: I think it is not so much pegging a certain level in the steady state, but rather, trying to find optimal conditions for us to be able to implement WFH in a sustainable manner.

sections.label: WFH affects wider ecosystem
sections.summary: Implementing WFH affects not just employers and employees but also the ecosystem of businesses and individuals supporting WFH and workplace arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Indeed, implementing WFH affects not just the employers and the employees, but also the eco-system – the businesses and the individuals supporting WFH as well as work from office, work from workplace arrangements.
